type: Three-day Power Stack rerank — Sep 8, Sep 9 and Sep 10 verified research
evidencePolicy: Theme and action rankings may move on independently verified macro, market and company evidence. Canonical holding fundamental scores remain unchanged unless stock-specific earnings, balance-sheet, cash-flow, business-quality, growth or valuation evidence changes. Transcript material remains zero-weight discovery input.
regime: Inflationary physical scarcity and record power demand are colliding with restrictive long-end yields, weak breadth and rising AI funding burden. Prefer cash-generative scarcity, contracted/funded infrastructure and operating assets over financing-dependent duration. Positive earnings revisions remain the main broad-equity counterweight.
threeDayChange: Sep 8 established that Malaysia data-centre load is already observable, not merely projected, while copper and energy security strengthened and battery manufacturing overcapacity became a negative quality filter.

Sep 9 hardened the duration and commodity regime: crude, product shortages, copper and fertilizer moved together while the 10Y tested 4.8%, increasing the premium on cash conversion and funded backlog.

Sep 10 promoted refined products/shipping, global duration, AI financing quality, LNG rerouting and gold reserve diversification. Breadth is a fragility overlay, not a crash call, because forward earnings revisions remain constructive.

The portfolio-level implication is to separate physical demand from financing quality: power/grid demand can strengthen while high-duration developers, software and leveraged capital structures weaken.

holdingsActionRanking.reason: Integrated upstream, refining and LNG exposure captures the current crude/product/LNG regime while balance-sheet and cash-flow quality reduce duration sensitivity. Do not chase the geopolitical premium.
Tanker, shipping and energy-logistics stress strengthened materially over the last three days. Yinson transaction funding remains the main reason this does not become an add.

holdingsActionRanking.action: HOLD / SELECTIVE ADD ONLY ON DISCIPLINED SETUP
holdingsActionRanking.reason: Direct realised-price leverage to $100+ Brent is useful, but the current theme is increasingly products/shipping rather than crude alone and the conflict premium remains reversible.

holdingsActionRanking.action: HOLD / STRUCTURAL POWER THESIS; FUNDING SCREEN
holdingsActionRanking.reason: Record Malaysia data-centre load and global power demand validate the mechanism. High long yields, copper and project capex make contracted utilisation and FCF conversion the gating variables.
Elite franchise quality remains intact, but cash economics are catalyst-dated and high real yields make the current support/reclaim structure important.
Storage/VPP economics fit the power-scarcity regime, but autonomy duration, auto financing sensitivity, battery manufacturing overcapacity and unresolved Cybercab regulation keep the hurdle high.
High oil improves customer budgets but no new operating evidence repairs utilisation and work-order conversion. Macro tailwind cannot substitute for company execution.
Parent fundamentals are constructive but strike, expiry, liquidity and time decay can dominate the linked instrument; no standalone rating is fabricated.

watchlistRerankPrinciples: Promote operating assets and funded backlog ahead of requested MW or pre-revenue concepts.
Promote LNG, product shipping and gas-power equipment because the Gulf shock now transmits through global gas and refined products, not crude alone.
Raise gold as strategic diversification but retain real-yield entry discipline.
Keep refiners high conviction but below less-extended opportunities because product scarcity is increasingly priced.
Lower duration/liquidity beta and leveraged speculative structures while 10Y/real yields and weak-end credit remain restrictive.

adjacentIdeas.name: GE Vernova
adjacentIdeas.theme: Gas power + electrification + grid equipment + data-centre power
adjacentIdeas.whyNow: Q2 2026 orders reached $24.2B, backlog $176B, free cash flow $5.1B and data-centre orders exceeded $5B YTD. The business directly monetises the Power Stack split between record physical load and funded equipment backlog.
adjacentIdeas.risk: Premium valuation, Wind losses and execution/capacity expansion risk. Require a fresh price/retest before action.

adjacentIdeas.name: Baker Hughes
adjacentIdeas.theme: LNG equipment + gas turbines + data-centre power + thermal management
adjacentIdeas.whyNow: Q2 IET orders were $7.1B with record $37.1B IET RPO; awards span Venture Global, Cheniere and 1.3GW of mobile gas turbines for data-centre/oil-and-gas applications. Chart adds thermal-management and gas-handling exposure, making BKR a multi-theme beneficiary of LNG rerouting and time-to-power.
adjacentIdeas.risk: Chart integration, acquisition leverage, hydrogen weakness and timing volatility in LNG equipment orders.

adjacentIdeas.name: Scorpio Tankers
adjacentIdeas.whyNow: Q3 contracted LR2 spot/pool TCE was about $64,900/day as of Sep 3, while new multi-year charter-outs lock part of the current rate environment. This is a direct operating expression of the refined-product/shipping bottleneck rather than a crude-price proxy.
adjacentIdeas.risk: Tanker-rate mean reversion, de-escalation, fleet supply and convertible dilution. Do not extrapolate wartime rates permanently.

adjacentIdeas.name: nVent Electric
adjacentIdeas.theme: Electrical protection + liquid cooling + data-centre infrastructure
adjacentIdeas.whyNow: nVent is expanding liquid-cooling manufacturing for the third time in three years, adding more than 400,000 square feet of capacity. This is a narrower, component-level beneficiary of the cooling and electrical bottlenecks highlighted by record AI power demand.
adjacentIdeas.risk: Execution on capacity additions, acquisition integration and valuation sensitivity if AI infrastructure spending slows.

adjacentIdeas.name: Williams Companies
adjacentIdeas.theme: US gas pipelines + Gulf Coast LNG + power demand
adjacentIdeas.whyNow: Q2 adjusted EBITDA rose and guidance increased after the Momentum Midstream acquisition, directly connecting Haynesville supply to Gulf Coast LNG and power demand.
adjacentIdeas.risk: A Sep 9 federal court decision vacated a key New Jersey permit for the NESE project. The company says timing is unchanged, but permitting risk prevents top-tier promotion today.

notPromoted: Pre-revenue nuclear/SMR concepts: strategic nuclear demand is strong, but duration and funding conditions favour CCJ/BWXT/operating generation over project-finance optionality.
Additional commodity battery/lithium capacity: ESS deployment is strong but China manufacturing overcapacity remains a negative quality filter.
Broad high-duration software: earnings quality can be good, but the current relative-value hurdle versus physical scarcity and Treasury yields remains high.
Williams is kept in research queue until the NESE permit risk is resolved or sufficiently bounded.
